exclusions_of_note.name: Products/Completed Operations Aggregate — EXCLUDED
exclusions_of_note.impact: The Dec page shows the Products/Completed Operations Aggregate Limit as 'Excluded.' The Schedule of Underlying Insurance also shows the underlying Pekin GL Products/Completed Operations Aggregate as 'EXCLUDED.' For a company with 'Aero' in its name and a Phoenix manufacturing address, this is a critical structural gap: any products-completed operations claim has no excess attachment because there is no products coverage on the umbrella, AND because the underlying does not appear to provide products coverage either, the umbrella has nothing to follow form to. A separate dedicated Products Liability / Aviation Products policy is the appropriate remedy if Precision Aero manufactures or distributes aerospace components.

exclusions_of_note.name: Aircraft Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Excludes BI/PD arising out of ownership, maintenance, operation, use, loading/unloading, or entrustment to others of aircraft owned by any insured or chartered without crew. For an aerospace-named insured, ground operations involving aircraft (test flights, deliveries, hangar movements, ferry pilots) could trigger this. A standalone Aviation/Aircraft Liability policy is the appropriate remedy.

exclusions_of_note.name: Total Pollution Exclusion (with hostile-fire carve-back only)
exclusions_of_note.impact: Absolute pollution exclusion at premises owned/rented/occupied; sites used for waste handling/storage; sites where pollutants are brought on by the insured or its contractors; and governmental cleanup directives. Only carve-back is heat/smoke/fumes from a hostile fire. Aerospace manufacturing typically uses solvents, fuels, lubricants, and chemicals — a Contractors Pollution Liability or Premises Pollution Liability policy would be the appropriate remedy for environmental exposures.

exclusions_of_note.name: Professional Liability Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Excludes any damages because of 'professional liability' as broadly defined in Section V.15 (engineers, architects, surveyors, draftsmen explicitly listed). For a manufacturer doing engineered components or design work, this is a hard exclusion. A standalone Professional/E&O or Manufacturers E&O policy is the appropriate remedy.

exclusions_of_note.name: Cyber / Access or Disclosure of Confidential Information / Data-Related Liability
exclusions_of_note.impact: Absolute cyber exclusion. Bars BI, PD, Personal Injury, AND Advertising Injury arising from any access to or disclosure of personal/confidential information, biometric data, or any electronic data loss/corruption. Endorsement is the version WITHOUT the limited bodily-injury exception — meaning even a BI claim traceable to a cyber event is excluded. A standalone Cyber Liability policy is required.

exclusions_of_note.name: Wrap-Up (OCIP/CCIP) Exclusion — Designated Operations
exclusions_of_note.impact: Excludes BI/PD arising out of ongoing ops or products-completed operations at any wrap-up location, regardless of whether the wrap-up is in effect, has adequate limits, or provides identical coverage. If Precision Aero performs work at a customer/owner-controlled construction site under an OCIP/CCIP, no umbrella coverage exists — including for completed operations after the wrap-up's tail expires. The insured must rely solely on the wrap-up policy and its sunset provisions.

exclusions_of_note.name: Watercraft Over 50 Feet Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Excludes watercraft over 50 feet; watercraft 50 feet or less is covered only if covered by underlying and 'no broader than the underlying.' Likely not material for this insured but a structural limit.

exclusions_of_note.name: ERISA / Employee Benefits / Fiduciary Liability Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Excludes any liability (including fiduciary) from employee benefit plans, ERISA, Pension Reform Act. A standalone Fiduciary Liability policy and Employee Benefits Liability endorsement on the underlying GL are the appropriate remedies.

exclusions_of_note.name: Insured-vs-Insured (Claim by Named Insured against Named Insured)
exclusions_of_note.impact: Bars any claim brought 'by or on behalf of you or any additional Named Insured.' Cross-suits between affiliated entities listed on the umbrella receive no coverage. Material when the program later adds subsidiaries — they cannot sue each other under this umbrella.

exclusions_of_note.name: Discrimination Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: 'Any alleged or actual discrimination by an insured against any person.' EPLI-type claims have no umbrella excess. A standalone EPLI policy is the appropriate remedy.

exclusions_of_note.name: Damage to Property Owned/Rented/Occupied; Care, Custody and Control
exclusions_of_note.impact: Excludes property damage to property owned, rented, occupied, loaned to insured, or in care/custody/control. Standard but worth noting — Bailee or Inland Marine coverage is the appropriate remedy.

exclusions_of_note.name: Certified Acts of Terrorism (and Other Acts Outside US over thresholds)
exclusions_of_note.impact: Insured rejected TRIA. Certified acts of terrorism, and large-scale 'other acts of terrorism' committed outside the US (>$25M property damage, ≥50 deaths/serious injury, NBC-related, etc.) are excluded.

exclusions_of_note.name: Punitive Damages from Certified Acts of Terrorism
exclusions_of_note.impact: Punitive damages tied to certified terrorism are excluded.

structural_notes.follow_form_type: Conditional follow form — Section I.1.b(1) caps payment at the part of ultimate net loss exceeding underlying limits; Section II.6 limits AI coverage to 'no broader than that of the underlying insurance.' This is a textbook conditional follow-form umbrella with the well-known traps when underlying has been endorsed for PNC, Waiver of Subrogation, or Notice/Knowledge but the umbrella has not been similarly endorsed.
schedule_of_underlying_blanks: Professional Liability — NOT listed (no follow-form excess for any E&O the insured may carry)
Cyber Liability — NOT listed (and Coverage A/B excludes cyber via CU 00 56 anyway)
Pollution Liability — NOT listed (and pollution is excluded outright)
underlying_listed: Pekin GL 006206676 — $1M occurrence / $2M general aggregate / Products-Completed Ops EXCLUDED / $1M Personal & Advertising
Pekin Auto — $1M CSL (also broken out as $1M BI/person, $1M BI/accident, $1M PD/accident)
structural_notes.other_insurance_clause: Section IV.9 — bare excess over underlying and any other collectible insurance; no Primary & Non-Contributory giveback. If the underlying GL is endorsed PNC for an AI, the umbrella will NOT follow that endorsement and will sit excess of any other valid and collectible insurance — a classic conditional-follow-form gap.
structural_notes.transfer_of_rights_of_recovery: Section IV.8 — standard subrogation language; no Waiver of Subrogation giveback. If the underlying carries a blanket Waiver of Subrogation endorsement, the umbrella does NOT follow form to that waiver.
structural_notes.notice_and_knowledge: Section IV.6 — broad 'you must see to it that we... are notified as soon as practicable' language with no carve-back limiting knowledge to the person responsible for insurance. Standard poorly constructed term flagged in Book of Solutions Umbrella.
structural_notes.maintenance_of_underlying: Section IV.10 — favorable wording: failure to maintain does NOT invalidate the umbrella, but the umbrella applies as though underlying were in force at scheduled limits (i.e., umbrella does not drop down to fill the gap). Insured still bears the gap if they let underlying lapse or reduce limits.
structural_notes.defense_costs: Supplementary Payments are payable IN ADDITION to the limit of insurance (Section I.3). Defense costs treatment is favorable (outside limits) when the umbrella defends; however the umbrella only has a duty to defend when no underlying applies or underlying aggregate has been exhausted by paid losses.
